recipe_version.title: Chilean Porotos Granados: Bean, Squash, and Corn Stew with Pebre
recipe_version.description: Chile's summer stew of cranberry beans, butternut squash that melts into the broth, and sweet corn, seasoned with paprika, oregano, and lots of fresh basil. Topped with pebre, a bright cilantro, tomato, and chile salsa.

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Peel and cube the squash. Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Drain and rinse the beans. For the pebre, dice the tomato and red onion, chop the cilantro, and mince the jalapeño.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.body: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in the Dutch oven over medium. Cook the onion until soft, 5 minutes; add the garlic, paprika, and oregano for 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer the squash
steps.body: Add the squash, 3 cups water, and 1 3/4 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered on medium-low until the squash is very soft, 20 minutes. Mash about a third of the squash against the side of the pot to thicken the stew.

steps.title: Make the pebre
steps.body: While the squash simmers, stir the tomato, red onion, cilantro, jalapeño, vinegar, 1 tbsp olive oil, and 1/4 tsp salt together. Runs inside step 3 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Add beans and corn
steps.body: Stir in the beans and corn and simmer 10 minutes, until the corn is tender and the stew is thick.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.body: Off the heat, stir in most of the basil. Ladle into bowls, top with pebre and the remaining basil.
